result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.rev_edge_dir_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Reverse the direction of all selected edges (directed graphs only). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23047-L23156){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.rev_edge_dir_ws() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Reverse selected edges](/assets/graphs/rev-edge-dir-ws.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a directed six-node graph with edges B→C and D→E selected in the accent color. Right: the same two edges now point the other way, C→B and E→D, still in the accent color; every other edge keeps its direction." width="100%"} For each selected edge (A->B), changes it to (B->A). Edge IDs and all attributes (including weights) are preserved during reversal. Only the direction is changed. The method works on the current edge selection (the `_ws` suffix means "with selection"), so it is usually chained after `select_edges()` or `select_edges_by_id()`. Node selections are ignored, and unselected edges keep their direction. The graph is modified in place. Typical uses: - fixing edges that were imported or entered the wrong way round - switching the meaning of a relationship, e.g., from "depends on" to "is required by", for part of a graph - reorienting a subset of edges before a direction-sensitive analysis such as a topological sort or reachability query Reversal does not check for an existing edge in the opposite direction: reversing `A->B` when `B->A` already exists leaves two parallel `B->A` edges. To keep the original edge and add its mirror image instead, use `add_reverse_edges_ws()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected (undirected edges have no direction to reverse). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Reversal is an in-place edit rather than a delete-then-insert: the underlying edge ID is preserved along with every attribute and weight, so downstream references remain valid. The selection state carries through unchanged, which makes `rev_edge_dir_ws()` chainable with further transformations. Requires a directed graph, since undirected edges have no direction to reverse. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~add_reverse_edges_ws`) : Add a reverse edge alongside each selected edge. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Reversing the single edge `A->B` turns it into `B->A`. The edge keeps its ID, so looking it up again gives the swapped endpoints, `(2, 1)`: ::: {#5309e943 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_node("A") graph.add_node("B") graph.add_edge("A", "B", weight=1.5) # Reverse the edge direction edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids() graph.select_edges_by_id([edge_ids[0]]) graph.rev_edge_dir_ws() # Edge now goes B -> A source, target = graph.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(edge_ids[0]) # Returns B -> A (source and target node IDs) (source, target) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (2, 1) ``` ::: ::: The weight is carried over unchanged: ::: {#87b7af2a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Weight is preserved edge = graph.get_edge(edge_ids[0]) # Returns 1.5 edge.weight ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1.5 ``` ::: ::: Flipping just the two later edges of a 4-node path changes the flow direction only in that part of the path, while `1->2` is left alone: ::: {#6b4c3699 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_path_graph(4) # 1->2->3->4 # Reverse the second and third edges edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids()[1:3] graph.select_edges_by_id(edge_ids) graph.rev_edge_dir_ws() graph.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['1->2', '3->2', '4->3'] ``` ::: :::
